history.period: Mainly 17th to 19th century; Maulikshya shrine claimed over 1,000 years old (unverified)
history.summary: Historic cluster of terracotta temples in Maluti village near Shikaripara, Dumka district, on the banks of the Chila river at the Bengal border. The Baj Basanta kings - founded by Basanta Roy, who received the tax-free 'Nankar Raj' from Sultan Alauddin Husain Shah of Gaur (1495-1525) for returning his hawk (Baj), hence 'Baj Basanta' - built temples instead of palaces, with four family branches building competitively. Of the original 108 temples (within ~350 m), 72 survive in semi-dilapidated condition. Bengal-style terracotta walls carry Ramayana scenes and local tribal-life motifs; inscriptions in early Bengali name them after female deities. Global Heritage Fund listed the site among the world's 12 most endangered cultural heritage sites. Known as 'Kashi of Jharkhand' / 'Gupta Kashi'. CSV state error: CSV column holds town 'Dumka'; actual state is Jharkhand. Coordinates are town-level (Wikipedia: 24.150 N, 87.667 E), not POI.

name: Maluti Temple Complex
town_description: Maluti is a small heritage village on the banks of the Chila river in Shikaripara block, Dumka district, near the West Bengal border (~55 km from Dumka town, ~16 km from Rampurhat in Birbhum). Its name traces to the Malla kings of Bishnupur, whose artisans built the terracotta temples. Largely rural and forested, the village survives as a pilgrimage-cum-heritage site with basic facilities; most visitors stay in Dumka or Rampurhat.

travel.airport: Deoghar Airport, about 120 km; Birsa Munda Airport, Ranchi, about 280-300 km by road.
travel.railway: Rampurhat (West Bengal), about 16 km - nearest; Dumka Junction, about 55 km.
travel.road: Bus and taxi from Rampurhat and Dumka; Maluti is 55 km from Dumka town on rural roads.
